prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1136; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by phone this morning after a hit while turning left at an intersection, with the claimant describing a neck strain and pain since the impact. Claimant is represented by counsel, so all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photos submitted with the file, which confirm some of the details described, including the position of the vehicles after the collision. No independent witnesses have come forward, but the responding officer's report places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene.

Entry 3: Vehicle damage to the front quarter panel and bumper lines up with the impact described by the claimant and the angle of the turn. Appraiser's notes support the repair estimate as presented.

Entry 4: Confirmed with the policy records that the driver lives with the named policyholder and is covered as a household member under the policy. No issues with coverage eligibility at this stage.

Entry 5: Checked the vehicle's prior claims and inspection history and found no earlier damage to the same areas. Nothing in the file suggests the damage occurred before the coverage period began.

Entry 6: Obtained the initial treatment records. The injury reported, a neck strain, fits the kind and force expected from this type of collision.

Entry 7: Claimant's medical history shows no earlier injury to the neck or upper back. Treatment has followed a usual course so far, with the frequency of visits decreasing as symptoms improved.

Entry 8: Spoke with the claimant again through counsel. The account of the collision matched what was given in the first report and in each prior conversation, with no changes in the sequence of events.

Entry 9: Reviewed the latest treatment notes. Progress has been steady, the claimant reports less pain and reduced stiffness, and the provider is tapering the plan toward discharge.

Entry 10: Updated the reserve to reflect the current treatment course and repair estimate. File remains open pending receipt of the final treatment summary and the attorney's demand package.
